name: Saint Peter Julian Eymard
history: A French priest of the Alps whose life was drawn ever more strongly to the Eucharist. After years as a Marist he founded the Congregation of the Blessed Sacrament in Paris in 1856, a community of priests and brothers devoted to perpetual adoration, and a sister congregation of women. He is remembered as the apostle of the Eucharist.
life: Peter Julian was born at La Mure, near Grenoble, the son of a cutler. His father opposed his vocation and his health was poor, but he was ordained for the diocese of Grenoble in 1834 and five years later joined the newly founded Society of Mary. As a Marist superior at Lyon he came to believe that Christ in the Eucharist deserved a community wholly given to Him. With the approval of the Archbishop of Paris he founded the Congregation of the Blessed Sacrament in Paris in 1856, and in 1858, with Marguerite Guillot, the Servants of the Blessed Sacrament. He began perpetual exposition in Paris, prepared poor adult workers for their First Communion, and wrote much on prayer before the Blessed Sacrament. Worn out, he died in his home town on 1 August 1868. John XXIII canonised him in 1962, during the Second Vatican Council.
prayerTo: Saint Peter Julian, you found in the Eucharist the centre of your life and longed for Christ to be adored in every place. Pray that I may come to Him often, kneel before Him with faith, and receive Him with love. Teach me to make my whole day an act of thanksgiving. Amen.
penance: Spend half an hour in adoration today, or a few quiet minutes before a tabernacle, and offer it for priests.
meditation: He taught that adoration is not idleness but the most fruitful work of all. What would it mean to bring one real concern of today to Christ in the tabernacle and simply leave it there?
